title: Fit an accessible toilet's two grab bars where ADA 604.5 puts them
instruction: This floor plan of an accessible toilet room is drawn at 1 in = 4 mm. The grey kerbs are the rear wall behind the toilet and the side wall beside it; the white shapes are the toilet's bowl and tank. Fit the two grab bars (40 in and 48 in long), one on each wall, where the 2010 ADA Standards require them for this toilet. Lay each bar flat on the floor along its wall, about 1-1/2 in off the kerb, then let go of both.
context: Carpenters, maintenance workers and building inspectors (O*NET 47-2031.00, 49-9071.00, 47-4011.00) fit and check grab bars in accessible toilet rooms to the 2010 ADA Standards. Section 604.5 sets them from the toilet, not by eye: the side-wall bar is at least 42 in long, starts at most 12 in from the rear wall and reaches at least 54 in out from it; the rear-wall bar is at least 36 in long and runs from the toilet's centreline at least 12 in toward the side wall and at least 24 in toward the open side, where a wheelchair user transfers. Two common errors are the shorter bar on the side wall and a rear bar centred on the toilet, which leaves the transfer side short. Here the room is drawn at 1 in = 4 mm with the toilet's centreline 17 in from the side wall (604.2 allows 16 to 18 in), and each bar starts parallel to the wrong wall, so which bar goes where and how far the rear bar is offset have to be worked out from the code.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height and stands for the room's floor. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A floor plan of an accessible single-user toilet room, drawn at 1 in = 4 mm (1:6.35), lies on the right half of the table; the room is open toward the arms (-x) and to the left (+y). (1) Rear wall: a fixed grey-painted wooden kerb, 10 mm wide (x), 330 mm long (y) and 4 mm tall, glued to the table at x 45.5 to 46.5 cm, y -32.5 to +0.5 cm; its face toward the room is at x 45.5 cm. (2) Side wall: a fixed grey-painted wooden kerb, 250 mm long (x), 10 mm wide (y) and 4 mm tall, at x 20.5 to 45.5 cm, y -32.5 to -31.5 cm, ending against the rear kerb's face; its face toward the room is at y -31.5 cm. (3) Toilet: two fixed vinyl shapes 0.5 mm thick stuck to the table, 72 mm (18 in) wide and centred on the toilet's centreline at y -24.7 cm (17 in, 68 mm, from the side wall's face): the tank, a pale grey-white rectangle 40 mm (x) by 72 mm (y) against the rear wall's face (x 41.5 to 45.5 cm, y -28.3 to -21.1 cm), and the bowl, a white disc 72 mm across centred at x 37.9 cm, y -24.7 cm, touching the tank's front edge (x 34.3 to 41.5 cm); the toilet is 112 mm (28 in) deep. No centreline is drawn. (4) Two loose grab bars of brushed aluminium square tube, 20 x 20 mm with a 1.5 mm wall and capped ends, lying flat on the floor: the 48 in bar, 192 mm long, 58 g, centred at x 24.0 cm, y -12.0 cm with its length along y, parallel to the rear wall (x 23.0 to 25.0 cm, y -21.6 to -2.4 cm); the 40 in bar, 160 mm long, 48 g, centred at x 35.0 cm, y -6.0 cm with its length along x, parallel to the side wall (x 27.0 to 43.0 cm, y -7.0 to -5.0 cm). The bars' four long faces are alike and their two ends are alike. At scale the kerbs stand for walls and the bars for 48 in and 40 in grab bars; their 20 mm section (5 in at scale) is over-scale so a gripper can hold them. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged on the end state from the bars' poses and both grippers (in a real trial: a tape from each kerb's face and a top photo). Scale 1 in = 4 mm; the toilet's centreline is at y -24.7 cm. A bar is 'along the side wall' when it lies flat on the floor (one of its long faces within 5 degrees of facing down and its lowest point within 3 mm of the table top: a bar on a kerb, on the other bar or on an end does not count), its length is within 5 degrees of parallel to the side kerb, its wall-side face is 0 to 15 mm from the kerb's face at the bar's midpoint (about 1-1/2 in is 6 mm, ADA 609.3; pressed against the kerb counts) and both its ends are beside the kerb (within 5 mm of x 20.5 to 45.5 cm). 'Along the rear wall' is the same with the rear kerb (ends within 5 mm of y -31.5 to +0.5 cm). A bar parallel to one wall cannot be along the other. A bar counts only when let go and settled: both grippers' finger zones at least 10 mm from it at every control step of the last 0.5 s (a finger zone: everything within reach of a pad's outer corner, half the finger gap plus 8 mm out and 13.5 mm across, round the 38 mm stretch back from the point between the pad tips, at any heading), and its centre moved under 2 mm in all and its heading under 1 degree in the last 0.5 s. 'Still for 1 s': settled in each of the last two 0.5 s. A bar's ends are its centre plus and minus half its length along it. Each wall is judged by the 2010 ADA Standards, whichever bar is on it. The side wall is compliant (604.5.1) if a counted bar along it is at least 42 in (168 mm) long, its rear end at most 12 in (48 mm) from the rear wall's face and its front end at least 54 in (216 mm) from it. The rear wall is compliant (604.5.2) if a counted bar along it is at least 36 in (144 mm) long, its end toward the side wall at least 12 in (48 mm) past the centreline (y -29.5 cm or less) and its other end at least 24 in (96 mm) past it toward the open side (y -15.1 cm or more). First match wins: both walls compliant and both bars still for 1 s, 1.0 (success; the trial ends once this has held 1 s). One wall compliant and a counted bar along the other wall (not compliant, or the 1.0 layout not yet still for 1 s), 0.75. One wall compliant and no counted bar along the other, 0.5. A counted bar along a wall but neither wall compliant, 0.25. No counted bar along either wall, 0 (nothing moved; bars held, moving, tilted, stacked, crosswise or over 15 mm off a kerb). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Examples: the 48 in bar on the side wall with its rear end 36 mm from the rear wall and the 40 in bar on the rear wall 12 mm off the side wall, 1.0; the same with the rear bar centred on the toilet (stopped by the side kerb it reaches only 23 in toward the open side), 0.75; the bars swapped (the 48 in bar meets the rear-wall rule, the 40 in bar is under 42 in), 0.75; the side bar right and the 40 in bar left where it started, 0.5; both bars along their walls with the side bar's rear end over 12 in from the rear wall and the rear bar centred, 0.25; a bar the gripper still holds does not count. Otherwise the last step is scored.
fidelity: A floor-plan mock-up at 1 in = 4 mm: the walls are 4 mm kerbs, the toilet is painted, and the bars lie on the floor along their walls instead of being fixed 33 to 36 in up on brackets, so mounting height and fixing strength are not tested. Lengths along the walls, which 604.5 sets, are to scale. The bars' 20 mm section is over-scale and simulated as solid boxes of the tube's mass. The scorer reads the bars' poses and each gripper's position and opening, not contact.
reset_notes: Put the 48 in bar back flat on the floor centred at x 24.0 cm, y -12.0 cm with its length along y (parallel to the rear wall), and the 40 in bar flat centred at x 35.0 cm, y -6.0 cm with its length along x (parallel to the side wall). Either long face may be down and either end may point either way. The kerbs and the painted toilet are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
